subject: Draft: OKR gap-bridge playbook and leadership comms
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OKR gap-bridge proposal for QBR

Team —

I've done a quick pass on the numbers for this quarter and we have a set of OKRs where the forecast is materially behind plan (platform latency, model inference cost per 1k tokens, and enterprise renewals). Rather than a reactive firefight, I want us to put a short, transparent "gap-bridge" comm to execs and the broader org that: 1) acknowledges the delta, 2) explains root causes, and 3) outlines short-term mitigations + owners through the QBR window.

High-level ask: can Chloe and Marissa lead a comm draft for leadership review by EOD Wednesday? Karthik — can you confirm the engineering mitigations and owners (3-4 items max)? Naomi — we'd like a quick runbook for people managers to use during team syncs.

Attached: okr-gap-bridge-deck-v0.1.pdf (strawman slides)

Important constraints: keep it factual and avoid committing to timeframe changes without a rollout plan. This is an alignment-first note, not a public apology.

Thanks — will sync 11:30 if helpful.

Jonas
Head of Product
Redwood Inference
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR gap-bridge proposal for QBR

Thanks Jonas — I can take point on the comm draft and weave in the short-term mitigations. Proposed structure below; happy to iterate:

- One-paragraph summary for execs (what, why, immediate impact)
- Two-slide appendix: metrics and root-cause snapshot
- Action table: owner, ask, ETA (30/60/90 day tiers)
- Manager script + suggested talking points for team syncs

Timeline: I will circulate a first-pass comm + editable comm-template-v1.docx by 5pm PT Wednesday. Marissa — would you own the People Ops side of the manager script (how to surface concerns, where to escalate)? Karthik — please add engineering owners inline in the attached deck (slide 3). Naomi — can you book a 30-minute dry run for Fri 5/8 (target: leadership readout on Monday)?

Quick note on tone: we keep it blunt but calm — ownership, mitigation, and clear next steps. I attached a lightweight comm template; use it for the org email and the manager script.

Chloe Martin
Senior Director, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: comm-template-v1.docx (editable manager script + short exec note)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 11:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR gap-bridge proposal for QBR

Chloe — happy to take the manager script. A few quick asks:

- Include an FAQ stub for managers: likely Qs from ICs about hiring freezes/raises and how this affects performance goals.
- Add a short escalation path for people issues (who to contact for promotions/career conversations impacted by OKR shifts).

I've added two bullet points in the comm-template where managers can direct employees to people ops and to a dedicated Q&A doc (internal). Also copying Pearl Consulting (external-hr@pearl-consulting.com) since they may want to help with the manager guide wording.

Marissa
VP, People Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR gap-bridge proposal for QBR — dry run invite + final notes

Folks — I booked a 30-minute dry run for Fri 2026-05-08 10:00-10:30 PT (qbr-dryrun-invite.ics attached). Agenda: walkthrough comm note, manager script highlights, and a 10-minute Q&A on escalation mechanics.

Chloe — I'll merge everyone's comments into a single Google doc and post a link in #exec-comm. Please review the doc (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QBR-draft-okr-bridge) before the dry run; I'll lock comments 1 hour prior.

Karthik — quick engineering ask: if we can surface 1-2 immediate low-effort mitigations (e.g., small batch size tuning, short-lived reserve capacity) in the deck, that will help reduce perceived risk in the readout.

Naomi Feldman
Head of People Strategy
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: qbr-dryrun-invite.ics (calendar invite stub)
